title: chatcompletions-compat-gateway-schema-adaptor-for-toolstream
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight compatibility gateway that maps incoming OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request shapes and streaming responses to Redwood's canonical chat schema and back. Primary focus is correct mapping for: streamed deltas, function/tool calling (function call vs tools field), structured outputs (JSON/protocols), and preserving metadata needed by tooling (conversation_id, message_id, role/name).

Scope:
- Input mapping: Accept legacy OpenAI-style /v1/chat/completions request bodies (messages array, functions, function_call hints) and normalize to internal request model used by our runtime.
- Output mapping: Convert our canonical deltas (token/event framed) back into OpenAI-compatible SSE chunks and final responses; ensure function/tool call payloads match expected name/arguments shapes.
- Streaming: Support streaming SSE framing with delta compositions, ensure 'role', 'content', and 'function_call' chunks are emitted in a sequence compatible with common OpenAI clients. Handle early function_call emission vs full-generation function call decisions.
- Edge-cases: stop tokens mapping, truncated tool responses, model fallback when function signatures disagree, and idempotent retries.

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration tests covering 12 permutations: (tool present/absent) x (streaming/batched) x (structured-output/ freeform) x (name-as-role vs name-field).
- End-to-end QA with SDKs (node, python) reproduces legacy client behavior for function calls.
- Telemetry emits mapping events (mapping_version, mapping_path, coercions) for post-rollout debugging.
- Security review completed for potential injection surface in function_call.arguments when mapped from untrusted clients.

Design notes / mapping rules (summary):
- messages[] -> conversation messages: preserve role/name if provided. If OpenAI 'name' exists, map to message.metadata.author_name and set role="tool" if role="system/user/assistant" absent.
- functions[] (OpenAI) -> tools[] (Redwood): canonicalize schema types to our JSON-Schema-lite form. Store original 'function_id' in metadata for roundtrip.
- function_call: when streaming, emit event: {"delta_type":"function_call","name":"<fn>","arguments": "<partial|final>"} as SSE chunk with event: "function_call.delta". On finalization, emit a terminal chunk that includes "finish_reason":"function_call" and the reconciled arguments object.
- Streaming SSE composition: follow an ordering that avoids breaking existing client parsers: initial assistant.role token chunks -> content deltas -> function_call partials (if triggered early) -> finalization chunk. Each SSE chunk includes mapping_version header in metadata.
- Errors: return 4xx for schema validation failures with a machine-readable code and human message. Map internal runtime backoffs into OpenAI-compatible error codes for legacy clients.

Trade-offs considered:
- Option A: full fidelity roundtrip (preserve exact OpenAI shapes) is heavier and brittle across model versions.
- Option B (chosen): canonical internal model + stable mapping layer with explicit mapping_version and translation telemetry. Simpler to evolve runtime while keeping compatibility for clients.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind "compat-gateway-v2" for 2 weeks internal testing.
2) Canary for 5% of incoming OpenAI-compat traffic; monitor mapping_errors, function_call_mismatch, and latency delta.
3) Ramp to 50% after 72h if no regression; full rollout after 7 days and post-security sign-off.

Observability & QA:
- Dashboards: mapping_errors (by code), streaming_reorder_rate, function_call_mismatch_rate, sse_chunk_rate.
- E2E tests: harness linked below; replay recorded sessions from product team.

Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Chat+Compat+Gateway+Design, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7132, test harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-compat-tests
